export const namespaceAlias = Fx.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Fx.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: renamed named imports from "effect/Effect"
export const renamedImports = chain(getUser, (user) => mapSuccess(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: inside an Effect.gen body
export const insideGen = Effect.gen(function*() {
  const pair = yield* Effect.all([getUser, getOrders])
  return pair
})

// MUST TRIGGER: the inner effect declares its own `user` that shadows the outer
// parameter; it never references the outer binding (scope walk is by symbol, not by name)
export const shadowedName = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(
    Effect.sync(() => {
      const user = { id: "shadow" }
      return user.id
    }),
    (orders) => [user, orders] as const
  ))

// MUST TRIGGER: the inner effect reads a mutable binding only inside a nested
// function, so hoisting the inner effect does not change what it observes
let counter = 0
export const mutableReadInsideThunk = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(Effect.sync(() => counter), (count) => [user, count] as const))

// MUST TRIGGER (twice): two independent nested zips in the same expression
export const twoMatches = Effect.flatMap(
  Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const)),
  (pair) => Effect.map(fetchName, (name) => ({ pair, name }))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: already Effect.all
export const alreadyAll = Effect.all([getUser, getOrders])
export const alreadyAllRecord = Effect.all({ user: getUser, orders: getOrders })

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the inner effect references the outer binding (dependent effects)
export const dependentInner = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrdersFor(user.id), (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the outer binding is only referenced inside a nested thunk of the
// inner effect, but it is still a dependency (opencode `Scope.provide(..., scope)` near-miss)
export const dependentInnerThunk = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(Effect.sync(() => user.id.length), (length) => [user, length] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the outer binding is the second argument of the inner effect
// (opencode near-miss shape; Scope.extend is the v3 counterpart of Scope.provide)
declare const reserve: Effect.Effect<string, never, Scope.Scope>
export const dependentScopeExtend = Effect.flatMap(Scope.make(), (scope) =>
  Effect.map(Scope.extend(reserve, scope), (connection) => [scope, connection] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the outer binding is referenced only in a type position of the inner effect
export const dependentTypeReference = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(Effect.succeed<typeof user | undefined>(undefined), (maybe) => [user, maybe] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the combiner swaps the order (Effect.all([getOrders, getUser])
// would change the execution order)
export const swappedTuple = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [orders, user] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the record combiner lists the inner value first (rewriting would
// change either the execution order or the key order of the result)
export const swappedRecord = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ orders, user })))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the combiner does extra work
export const combinerDoesWork = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user.id, orders] as const))
export const combinerCallsFunction = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => `${user.id}:${orders.length}`))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the combiner has an extra element / property
export const tupleExtraElement = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders, 1] as const))
export const recordExtraProperty = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ user, orders, source: "db" })))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the combiner drops or duplicates a binding
export const tupleDuplicate = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (_orders) => [user, user] as const))
export const tupleSingle = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [orders] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: spread, computed key and method members are not a 1:1 record shape
export const recordSpread = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ ...user, orders })))
const userKey = "user"
export const recordComputedKey = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ [userKey]: user, orders })))
export const recordGetter = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({
    user,
    get orders() {
      return orders
    }
  })))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a type assertion other than `as const` changes the result type
export const tupleTypeAssertion = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as [User, ReadonlyArray<string>]))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: destructured outer / inner parameters are not simple bindings
export const destructuredOuter = Effect.flatMap(getUser, ({ id }) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [id, orders] as const))
export const destructuredInner = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, ([first]) => [user, first] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the outer callback has more than a single return of the inner map
export const outerBlockWithStatements = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => {
  const inner = getOrders
  return Effect.map(inner, (orders) => [user, orders] as const)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the inner map is not the returned expression of the outer callback
export const innerMapWrapped = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.asVoid(Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: hoisting the inner effect would read a mutable binding eagerly,
// once at construction instead of each time the outer effect succeeds
export const mutableReadEagerly = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(Effect.succeed(counter), (count) => [user, count] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: hoisting the inner effect would read a binding before its
// declaration (temporal dead zone)
export const declaredLater = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(laterOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))
const laterOrders = getOrders

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a `function` callback may rebind `this`; only arrow callbacks are matched
export const functionExpressionCallback = Effect.flatMap(getUser, function(user) {
  return Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the outer combinator is not Effect.flatMap
export const outerAndThen = Effect.andThen(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the inner combinator is not Effect.map
export const innerAndThen = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.andThen(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a single level of nesting (no inner map)
export const singleLevel = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.succeed([user] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Option.flatMap + Option.map (not the Effect module)
declare const maybeUser: Option.Option<User>
declare const maybeOrders: Option.Option<ReadonlyArray<string>>
export const optionPair = Option.flatMap(maybeUser, (user) =>
  Option.map(maybeOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Stream.flatMap + Stream.map (not the Effect module)
declare const users: Stream.Stream<User>
declare const orderStream: Stream.Stream<ReadonlyArray<string>>
export const streamPair = Stream.flatMap(users, (user) => Stream.map(orderStream, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: user-defined object whose methods are merely named flatMap / map
const custom = {
  flatMap: <A, B>(self: ReadonlyArray<A>, f: (a: A) => ReadonlyArray<B>): ReadonlyArray<B> => self.flatMap(f),
  map: <A, B>(self: ReadonlyArray<A>, f: (a: A) => B): ReadonlyArray<B> => self.map(f)
}
export const customPair = custom.flatMap([1, 2], (n) => custom.map(["a", "b"], (s) => [n, s] as const))

// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics zipViaNestedFlatMapToAll:warning
import { Clock, Effect, Option, pipe, Ref, Scope, Stream } from "effect"
import * as Fx from "effect/Effect"
import { flatMap as chain, map as mapSuccess } from "effect/Effect"

interface User {
  readonly id: string
}

declare const getUser: Effect.Effect<User>
declare const getOrders: Effect.Effect<ReadonlyArray<string>>
declare const getOrdersFor: (userId: string) => Effect.Effect<ReadonlyArray<string>>
declare const fetchCount: Effect.Effect<number, string, "Service">
declare const fetchName: Effect.Effect<string, Error>

// MUST TRIGGER: data-first flatMap + data-first map, `as const` tuple combiner
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders])
export const dataFirstTupleAsConst = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: plain tuple combiner (no `as const`)
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders])
export const dataFirstTuple = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders]))

// MUST TRIGGER: record combiner with shorthand properties
// fix: Effect.all({ user: getUser, orders: getOrders })
export const dataFirstRecordShorthand = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ user, orders })))

// MUST TRIGGER: record combiner with renamed keys
// fix: Effect.all({ owner: getUser, items: getOrders })
export const dataFirstRecordRenamed = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ owner: user, items: orders })))

// MUST TRIGGER: record combiner with string-literal keys
// fix: Effect.all({ "the-user": getUser, "the-orders": getOrders })
export const dataFirstRecordStringKeys = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ "the-user": user, "the-orders": orders })))

// MUST TRIGGER: pipeable outer flatMap + pipeable inner map (issue example)
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders])
export const pipeable = getUser.pipe(
  Effect.flatMap((user) =>
    getOrders.pipe(
      Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
    )
  )
)

// MUST TRIGGER: pipe(...) function style on both levels
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders])
export const functionPipe = pipe(
  getUser,
  Effect.flatMap((user) => pipe(getOrders, Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: pipeable outer, data-first inner
export const pipeableOuterDataFirstInner = getUser.pipe(
  Effect.flatMap((user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ user, orders })))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: data-first outer, pipeable inner
export const dataFirstOuterPipeableInner = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  getOrders.pipe(Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)))

// MUST TRIGGER: data-last call style on both levels
export const dataLast = Effect.flatMap((user: User) =>
  Effect.map((orders: ReadonlyArray<string>) => [user, orders] as const)(getOrders)
)(getUser)

// MUST TRIGGER: single-return block bodies on both callbacks
export const blockBodies = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => {
  return Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => {
    return [user, orders] as const
  })
})

// MUST TRIGGER: the inner effect is a call that does not reference the outer binding
// (real-world shape from Effect-TS/effect Sink.test.ts)
// fix: Effect.all([Stream.runCollect(Stream.make(1, 2, 3)), Ref.get(ref)])
export const independentCall = Effect.gen(function*() {
  const ref = yield* Ref.make(0)
  return yield* Effect.flatMap(Stream.runCollect(Stream.make(1, 2, 3)), (exit) =>
    Effect.map(Ref.get(ref), (result) => [exit, result] as const))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: record combiner over a module-level effect
// (real-world shape from pingdotgg/t3code PullRequestService.ts)
// fix: Effect.all({ result: fetchCount, at: Clock.currentTimeMillis })
export const clockRecord = fetchCount.pipe(
  Effect.flatMap((result) => Clock.currentTimeMillis.pipe(Effect.map((at) => ({ result, at }))))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: error and requirement channels differ between the two effects
export const mixedChannels = Effect.flatMap(fetchCount, (count) =>
  Effect.map(fetchName, (name) => [count, name] as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: the outer effect is an arbitrary expression (a call)
// fix: Effect.all([getOrdersFor("root"), getUser])
export const outerCall = Effect.flatMap(getOrdersFor("root"), (orders) =>
  Effect.map(getUser, (user) => [orders, user] as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: the outer flatMap is the last step of a longer flow
// fix: Effect.all([getUser.pipe(Effect.tap(...)), getOrders])
export const lastStepOfLongerFlow = getUser.pipe(
  Effect.tap((user) => Effect.log(user.id)),
  Effect.flatMap((user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: the outer flatMap sits in the middle of a flow; the fix replaces the
// flow up to the flatMap and keeps the later steps
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders]).pipe(Effect.map(...))
export const middleOfLongerFlow = getUser.pipe(
  Effect.flatMap((user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const)),
  Effect.map(([user, orders]) => `${user.id}:${orders.length}`)
)

// MUST TRIGGER: namespace import alias (resolved by symbol, not by name)

)(getUser)

// MUST TRIGGER: single-return block bodies on both callbacks
export const blockBodies = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => {
  return Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => {
    return [user, orders] as const
  })
})

// MUST TRIGGER: the inner effect is a call that does not reference the outer binding
// (real-world shape from Effect-TS/effect Sink.test.ts)
// fix: Effect.all([Stream.runCollect(Stream.make(1, 2, 3)), Ref.get(ref)])
export const independentCall = Effect.gen(function*() {
  const ref = yield* Ref.make(0)
  return yield* Effect.flatMap(Stream.runCollect(Stream.make(1, 2, 3)), (exit) =>
    Effect.map(Ref.get(ref), (result) => [exit, result] as const))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: record combiner over a module-level effect
// (real-world shape from pingdotgg/t3code PullRequestService.ts)
// fix: Effect.all({ result: fetchCount, at: Clock.currentTimeMillis })
export const clockRecord = fetchCount.pipe(
  Effect.flatMap((result) => Clock.currentTimeMillis.pipe(Effect.map((at) => ({ result, at }))))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: error and requirement channels differ between the two effects
export const mixedChannels = Effect.flatMap(fetchCount, (count) =>
  Effect.map(fetchName, (name) => [count, name] as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: the outer effect is an arbitrary expression (a call)
// fix: Effect.all([getOrdersFor("root"), getUser])
export const outerCall = Effect.flatMap(getOrdersFor("root"), (orders) =>
  Effect.map(getUser, (user) => [orders, user] as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: the outer flatMap is the last step of a longer flow
// fix: Effect.all([getUser.pipe(Effect.tap(...)), getOrders])
export const lastStepOfLongerFlow = getUser.pipe(
  Effect.tap((user) => Effect.log(user.id)),
  Effect.flatMap((user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: the outer flatMap sits in the middle of a flow; the fix replaces the
// flow up to the flatMap and keeps the later steps
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders]).pipe(Effect.map(...))
export const middleOfLongerFlow = getUser.pipe(
  Effect.flatMap((user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const)),
  Effect.map(([user, orders]) => `${user.id}:${orders.length}`)
)

// MUST TRIGGER: namespace import alias (resolved by symbol, not by name)
export const namespaceAlias = Fx.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Fx.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: renamed named imports from "effect/Effect"
export const renamedImports = chain(getUser, (user) => mapSuccess(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: inside an Effect.gen body
export const insideGen = Effect.gen(function*() {
  const pair = yield* Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))
  return pair
})

// MUST TRIGGER: the inner effect declares its own `user` that shadows the outer
// parameter; it never references the outer binding (scope walk is by symbol, not by name)
export const shadowedName = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(
    Effect.sync(() => {
      const user = { id: "shadow" }
      return user.id
    }),
    (orders) => [user, orders] as const
  ))

// MUST TRIGGER: the inner effect reads a mutable binding only inside a nested
// function, so hoisting the inner effect does not change what it observes
let counter = 0
export const mutableReadInsideThunk = Effect.all([getUser, Effect.sync(() => counter)])

// MUST TRIGGER (twice): two independent nested zips in the same expression
export const twoMatches = Effect.flatMap(
  Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const)),
  (pair) => Effect.map(fetchName, (name) => ({ pair, name }))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: already Effect.all
export const alreadyAll = Effect.all([getUser, getOrders])
export const alreadyAllRecord = Effect.all({ user: getUser, orders: getOrders })

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the inner effect references the outer binding (dependent effects)
export const dependentInner = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrdersFor(user.id), (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the outer binding is only referenced inside a nested thunk of the
// inner effect, but it is still a dependency (opencode `Scope.provide(..., scope)` near-miss)
export const dependentInnerThunk = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(Effect.sync(() => user.id.length), (length) => [user, length] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the outer binding is the second argument of the inner effect
// (opencode near-miss shape; Scope.extend is the v3 counterpart of Scope.provide)
declare const reserve: Effect.Effect<string, never, Scope.Scope>
export const dependentScopeExtend = Effect.flatMap(Scope.make(), (scope) =>
  Effect.map(Scope.extend(reserve, scope), (connection) => [scope, connection] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the outer binding is referenced only in a type position of the inner effect
export const dependentTypeReference = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(Effect.succeed<typeof user | undefined>(undefined), (maybe) => [user, maybe] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the combiner swaps the order (Effect.all([getOrders, getUser])
// would change the execution order)
export const swappedTuple = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [orders, user] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the record combiner lists the inner value first (rewriting would
// change either the execution order or the key order of the result)
export const swappedRecord = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ orders, user })))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the combiner does extra work
export const combinerDoesWork = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user.id, orders] as const))
export const combinerCallsFunction = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => `${user.id}:${orders.length}`))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the combiner has an extra element / property
export const tupleExtraElement = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders, 1] as const))
export const recordExtraProperty = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ user, orders, source: "db" })))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the combiner drops or duplicates a binding
export const tupleDuplicate = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (_orders) => [user, user] as const))
export const tupleSingle = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [orders] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: spread, computed key and method members are not a 1:1 record shape
export const recordSpread = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ ...user, orders })))
const userKey = "user"
export const recordComputedKey = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ [userKey]: user, orders })))
export const recordGetter = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({
    user,
    get orders() {
      return orders
    }
  })))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a type assertion other than `as const` changes the result type
export const tupleTypeAssertion = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as [User, ReadonlyArray<string>]))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: destructured outer / inner parameters are not simple bindings
export const destructuredOuter = Effect.flatMap(getUser, ({ id }) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [id, orders] as const))
export const destructuredInner = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, ([first]) => [user, first] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the outer callback has more than a single return of the inner map
export const outerBlockWithStatements = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => {
  const inner = getOrders
  return Effect.map(inner, (orders) => [user, orders] as const)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the inner map is not the returned expression of the outer callback
export const innerMapWrapped = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.asVoid(Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: hoisting the inner effect would read a mutable binding eagerly,
// once at construction instead of each time the outer effect succeeds
export const mutableReadEagerly = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(Effect.succeed(counter), (count) => [user, count] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: hoisting the inner effect would read a binding before its
// declaration (temporal dead zone)
export const declaredLater = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(laterOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))
const laterOrders = getOrders

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a `function` callback may rebind `this`; only arrow callbacks are matched
export const functionExpressionCallback = Effect.flatMap(getUser, function(user) {
  return Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the outer combinator is not Effect.flatMap
export const outerAndThen = Effect.andThen(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the inner combinator is not Effect.map
export const innerAndThen = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.andThen(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a single level of nesting (no inner map)
export const singleLevel = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.succeed([user] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Option.flatMap + Option.map (not the Effect module)
declare const maybeUser: Option.Option<User>
declare const maybeOrders: Option.Option<ReadonlyArray<string>>
export const optionPair = Option.flatMap(maybeUser, (user) =>
  Option.map(maybeOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Stream.flatMap + Stream.map (not the Effect module)
declare const users: Stream.Stream<User>
declare const orderStream: Stream.Stream<ReadonlyArray<string>>
export const streamPair = Stream.flatMap(users, (user) => Stream.map(orderStream, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: user-defined object whose methods are merely named flatMap / map
const custom = {
  flatMap: <A, B>(self: ReadonlyArray<A>, f: (a: A) => ReadonlyArray<B>): ReadonlyArray<B> => self.flatMap(f),
  map: <A, B>(self: ReadonlyArray<A>, f: (a: A) => B): ReadonlyArray<B> => self.map(f)
}
export const customPair = custom.flatMap([1, 2], (n) => custom.map(["a", "b"], (s) => [n, s] as const))

import * as Fx from "effect/Effect"
import { flatMap as chain, map as mapSuccess } from "effect/Effect"

interface User {
  readonly id: string
}

declare const getUser: Effect.Effect<User>
declare const getOrders: Effect.Effect<ReadonlyArray<string>>
declare const getOrdersFor: (userId: string) => Effect.Effect<ReadonlyArray<string>>
declare const fetchCount: Effect.Effect<number, string, "Service">
declare const fetchName: Effect.Effect<string, Error>

// MUST TRIGGER: data-first flatMap + data-first map, `as const` tuple combiner

  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: plain tuple combiner (no `as const`)
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders])
export const dataFirstTuple = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders]))

// MUST TRIGGER: record combiner with shorthand properties
// fix: Effect.all({ user: getUser, orders: getOrders })
export const dataFirstRecordShorthand = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ user, orders })))

// MUST TRIGGER: record combiner with renamed keys
// fix: Effect.all({ owner: getUser, items: getOrders })
export const dataFirstRecordRenamed = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ owner: user, items: orders })))

// MUST TRIGGER: record combiner with string-literal keys

export const dataFirstRecordStringKeys = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>

  getUser,

// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders])
export const dataFirstTupleAsConst = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: plain tuple combiner (no `as const`)
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders])
export const dataFirstTuple = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders]))

// MUST TRIGGER: record combiner with shorthand properties
// fix: Effect.all({ user: getUser, orders: getOrders })
export const dataFirstRecordShorthand = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ user, orders })))

// MUST TRIGGER: record combiner with renamed keys
// fix: Effect.all({ owner: getUser, items: getOrders })
export const dataFirstRecordRenamed = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ owner: user, items: orders })))

// MUST TRIGGER: record combiner with string-literal keys
// fix: Effect.all({ "the-user": getUser, "the-orders": getOrders })
export const dataFirstRecordStringKeys = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ "the-user": user, "the-orders": orders })))

// MUST TRIGGER: pipeable outer flatMap + pipeable inner map (issue example)
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders])
export const pipeable = getUser.pipe(
  Effect.flatMap((user) =>
    getOrders.pipe(
      Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
    )
  )
)

// MUST TRIGGER: pipe(...) function style on both levels
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders])
export const functionPipe = pipe(
  getUser,
  Effect.flatMap((user) => pipe(getOrders, Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: pipeable outer, data-first inner
export const pipeableOuterDataFirstInner = getUser.pipe(
  Effect.flatMap((user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ user, orders })))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: data-first outer, pipeable inner
export const dataFirstOuterPipeableInner = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  getOrders.pipe(Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)))

// MUST TRIGGER: data-last call style on both levels
export const dataLast = Effect.flatMap((user: User) =>
  Effect.map((orders: ReadonlyArray<string>) => [user, orders] as const)(getOrders)
)(getUser)

// MUST TRIGGER: single-return block bodies on both callbacks
export const blockBodies = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => {
  return Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => {
    return [user, orders] as const
  })
})

// MUST TRIGGER: the inner effect is a call that does not reference the outer binding
// (real-world shape from Effect-TS/effect Sink.test.ts)
// fix: Effect.all([Stream.runCollect(Stream.make(1, 2, 3)), Ref.get(ref)])
export const independentCall = Effect.gen(function*() {
  const ref = yield* Ref.make(0)
  return yield* Effect.flatMap(Stream.runCollect(Stream.make(1, 2, 3)), (exit) =>
    Effect.map(Ref.get(ref), (result) => [exit, result] as const))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: record combiner over a module-level effect
// (real-world shape from pingdotgg/t3code PullRequestService.ts)
// fix: Effect.all({ result: fetchCount, at: Clock.currentTimeMillis })
export const clockRecord = fetchCount.pipe(
  Effect.flatMap((result) => Clock.currentTimeMillis.pipe(Effect.map((at) => ({ result, at }))))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: error and requirement channels differ between the two effects
export const mixedChannels = Effect.flatMap(fetchCount, (count) =>
  Effect.map(fetchName, (name) => [count, name] as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: the outer effect is an arbitrary expression (a call)
// fix: Effect.all([getOrdersFor("root"), getUser])
export const outerCall = Effect.flatMap(getOrdersFor("root"), (orders) =>
  Effect.map(getUser, (user) => [orders, user] as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: the outer flatMap is the last step of a longer flow
// fix: Effect.all([getUser.pipe(Effect.tap(...)), getOrders])
export const lastStepOfLongerFlow = getUser.pipe(
  Effect.tap((user) => Effect.log(user.id)),
  Effect.flatMap((user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: the outer flatMap sits in the middle of a flow; the fix replaces the
// flow up to the flatMap and keeps the later steps
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders]).pipe(Effect.map(...))
export const middleOfLongerFlow = getUser.pipe(
  Effect.flatMap((user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const)),
  Effect.map(([user, orders]) => `${user.id}:${orders.length}`)
)

// MUST TRIGGER: namespace import alias (resolved by symbol, not by name)
export const namespaceAlias = Fx.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Fx.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: renamed named imports from "effect/Effect"
export const renamedImports = chain(getUser, (user) => mapSuccess(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: inside an Effect.gen body
export const insideGen = Effect.gen(function*() {
  const pair = yield* Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))
  return pair
})

// MUST TRIGGER: the inner effect declares its own `user` that shadows the outer
// parameter; it never references the outer binding (scope walk is by symbol, not by name)
export const shadowedName = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(
    Effect.sync(() => {
      const user = { id: "shadow" }
      return user.id
    }),
    (orders) => [user, orders] as const
  ))

// MUST TRIGGER: the inner effect reads a mutable binding only inside a nested
// function, so hoisting the inner effect does not change what it observes
let counter = 0
export const mutableReadInsideThunk = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(Effect.sync(() => counter), (count) => [user, count] as const))

// MUST TRIGGER (twice): two independent nested zips in the same expression
export const twoMatches = Effect.flatMap(
  Effect.all([getUser, getOrders]),
  (pair) => Effect.map(fetchName, (name) => ({ pair, name }))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: already Effect.all
export const alreadyAll = Effect.all([getUser, getOrders])
export const alreadyAllRecord = Effect.all({ user: getUser, orders: getOrders })

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the inner effect references the outer binding (dependent effects)
export const dependentInner = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrdersFor(user.id), (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the outer binding is only referenced inside a nested thunk of the
// inner effect, but it is still a dependency (opencode `Scope.provide(..., scope)` near-miss)
export const dependentInnerThunk = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(Effect.sync(() => user.id.length), (length) => [user, length] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the outer binding is the second argument of the inner effect
// (opencode near-miss shape; Scope.extend is the v3 counterpart of Scope.provide)
declare const reserve: Effect.Effect<string, never, Scope.Scope>
export const dependentScopeExtend = Effect.flatMap(Scope.make(), (scope) =>
  Effect.map(Scope.extend(reserve, scope), (connection) => [scope, connection] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the outer binding is referenced only in a type position of the inner effect
export const dependentTypeReference = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(Effect.succeed<typeof user | undefined>(undefined), (maybe) => [user, maybe] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the combiner swaps the order (Effect.all([getOrders, getUser])
// would change the execution order)
export const swappedTuple = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [orders, user] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the record combiner lists the inner value first (rewriting would
// change either the execution order or the key order of the result)
export const swappedRecord = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ orders, user })))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the combiner does extra work
export const combinerDoesWork = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user.id, orders] as const))
export const combinerCallsFunction = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => `${user.id}:${orders.length}`))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the combiner has an extra element / property
export const tupleExtraElement = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders, 1] as const))
export const recordExtraProperty = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ user, orders, source: "db" })))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the combiner drops or duplicates a binding
export const tupleDuplicate = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (_orders) => [user, user] as const))
export const tupleSingle = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [orders] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: spread, computed key and method members are not a 1:1 record shape
export const recordSpread = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ ...user, orders })))
const userKey = "user"
export const recordComputedKey = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ [userKey]: user, orders })))
export const recordGetter = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({
    user,
    get orders() {
      return orders
    }
  })))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a type assertion other than `as const` changes the result type
export const tupleTypeAssertion = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as [User, ReadonlyArray<string>]))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: destructured outer / inner parameters are not simple bindings
export const destructuredOuter = Effect.flatMap(getUser, ({ id }) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [id, orders] as const))
export const destructuredInner = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, ([first]) => [user, first] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the outer callback has more than a single return of the inner map
export const outerBlockWithStatements = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => {
  const inner = getOrders
  return Effect.map(inner, (orders) => [user, orders] as const)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the inner map is not the returned expression of the outer callback
export const innerMapWrapped = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.asVoid(Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: hoisting the inner effect would read a mutable binding eagerly,
// once at construction instead of each time the outer effect succeeds
export const mutableReadEagerly = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(Effect.succeed(counter), (count) => [user, count] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: hoisting the inner effect would read a binding before its
// declaration (temporal dead zone)
export const declaredLater = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(laterOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))
const laterOrders = getOrders

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a `function` callback may rebind `this`; only arrow callbacks are matched
export const functionExpressionCallback = Effect.flatMap(getUser, function(user) {
  return Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the outer combinator is not Effect.flatMap
export const outerAndThen = Effect.andThen(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the inner combinator is not Effect.map
export const innerAndThen = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.andThen(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a single level of nesting (no inner map)
export const singleLevel = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.succeed([user] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Option.flatMap + Option.map (not the Effect module)
declare const maybeUser: Option.Option<User>
declare const maybeOrders: Option.Option<ReadonlyArray<string>>
export const optionPair = Option.flatMap(maybeUser, (user) =>
  Option.map(maybeOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Stream.flatMap + Stream.map (not the Effect module)
declare const users: Stream.Stream<User>
declare const orderStream: Stream.Stream<ReadonlyArray<string>>
export const streamPair = Stream.flatMap(users, (user) => Stream.map(orderStream, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: user-defined object whose methods are merely named flatMap / map
const custom = {
  flatMap: <A, B>(self: ReadonlyArray<A>, f: (a: A) => ReadonlyArray<B>): ReadonlyArray<B> => self.flatMap(f),
  map: <A, B>(self: ReadonlyArray<A>, f: (a: A) => B): ReadonlyArray<B> => self.map(f)
}
export const customPair = custom.flatMap([1, 2], (n) => custom.map(["a", "b"], (s) => [n, s] as const))
